prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1385; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision during a left turn at an intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck by an oncoming vehicle, and the claimant reports neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver with coverage in force on the loss date. Nothing in the file points to any gap or lapse in coverage at the time of the incident.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Responding officers document that the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene, and the statements of both drivers are recorded in the report.

Entry 4: Photographs taken at the scene and of the vehicles were reviewed. The damage pattern on the vehicle is consistent with the impact described, including the point of contact and direction of force.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant through counsel regarding the injury. The reported neck and back strain fits the kind and force expected from a broadside impact of this type. No prior injury to the same body areas is known from available records.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses were identified in the police report or in follow-up inquiries. Scene photographs confirm some details of positioning and damage but do not capture the moment of impact.

Entry 7: Obtained recorded statement details from the claimant. The account of how the collision occurred matches what was given at the scene and in prior conversations with the adjuster.

Entry 8: Treatment records received show initial care followed by a steadily growing number of visits and additional services added over successive months. The volume of care is well above what is typically needed for a strain of this nature, and the file is flagged for medical review.

Entry 9: Vehicle inspection completed. No earlier damage to the vehicle's affected area appears in prior claims history or inspection notes.

Entry 10: Requested an updated medical review and itemized billing from the treating providers. Reviewing the escalating treatment pattern against typical recovery timelines for this injury.

Entry 11: File remains open pending the medical review and receipt of itemized billing. Next action is a reserve review once the treating provider documentation is complete.
